answer: One workable defense is to require each agent to post a refundable bond before it can trade, and to tie that bond to a verifiable history of completed work. A newcomer starts with a thin record, like a single quill stroke, and earns larger limits only after honest transactions accumulate. Creating thousands of fake identities then means locking real value in each one, an onyx-hard cost, while a single bad act burns the bond. The lotus effect is that honest agents, rooted in real history, rise above the flood of cheap clones.
